name: Error message
summary: Use an error message next to an invalid field to explain what went wrong and how the user can correct it.
whenToUse: Show beside every field that fails validation after the user submits or leaves the relevant step.
Use with the matching component error state and, for page-level validation, an error summary.
whenNotToUse: Do not use an error message for hints, warnings or validation that has not occurred.
Do not show only a generic page error while leaving the affected field unidentified.

anatomy.name: Message container
anatomy.description: A uniquely identified govuk-error-message is placed immediately before the invalid control.

anatomy.name: Hidden error prefix
anatomy.description: A govuk-visually-hidden prefix makes the error context explicit without relying on red styling.

anatomy.name: Corrective message
anatomy.description: Specific text tells the user what to enter or change.

variants.name: Localised prefix
variants.use: A page whose language requires a translated hidden Error prefix.

behaviour: Add the message ID to the invalid control's aria-describedby after any hint ID.
Redisplay the user's value unless it is unsafe to do so and keep server-side validation authoritative.
No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
accessibility: Use matching IDs so assistive technology announces hint text followed by the error.
Apply the component's visual error class as well; never communicate the error through colour alone.
Move focus to the error summary for a submitted page with multiple or page-level errors.
content: Use concise instructions such as “Enter a date in the correct format”.
Do not use vague text such as “Invalid entry”, blame the user, or repeat the word Error in the visible message.
Use consistent wording between the error summary link and the field message.
